Amos 5:1.text: Hear this word of the Lord that I take up over you as a lament, house of Israel:

Amos 5:2.text: “Virgin Israel has fallen; she will certainly not rise again. She stumbled upon her land; no one will raise her.”

Amos 5:3.text: For thus says the Lord, the Lord: “From the city out of which a thousand went, a hundred will remain, and from the one out of which a hundred went, ten will remain for Israel’s house.”

Amos 5:4.text: For thus says the Lord to Israel’s house: “Seek Me and you will live!

Amos 5:5.text: Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to the Well of the Oath; for Gilgal will certainly be taken captive, and Bethel will be as though it did not exist.”

Amos 5:6.text: Seek the Lord and live, so that Joseph’s house does not flare up like fire; it will devour him, and there will be no one to quench it for Israel’s house.

Amos 5:7.text: The Lord makes judgment on high and has placed righteousness upon the earth,

Amos 5:8.text: making all things and refashioning them, turning death’s shadow into morning and darkening day into night; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name,

Amos 5:9.text: the One distributing shattering against strength and bringing suffering upon a fortress.

Amos 5:10.text: They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.

Amos 5:11.text: Therefore, because you struck the poor with fists and accepted choice gifts from them, you built houses of polished stone but certainly will not inhabit them; you planted desirable vineyards but certainly will not drink their wine.

Amos 5:12.text: For I knew your many impieties, and your sins are strong: trampling the righteous, taking payments and turning aside the poor at the gates.

Amos 5:13.text: Therefore the understanding person will be silent at that time, because it is an evil time.

Amos 5:14.text: Seek the good and not the evil, so that you may live; then the Lord God Almighty will be with you, just as you said,

Amos 5:15.text: “We have hated evil things and loved good things.” Restore judgment at the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on Joseph’s remaining ones.

Amos 5:16.text: Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: “In every square there will be mourning, and in every road it will be said, ‘Alas, alas!’ A farmer will be called to mourning and lamentation and to those skilled in wailing,

Amos 5:17.text: and in every road there will be mourning, because I will pass through your midst,” said the Lord.

Amos 5:18.text: Woe to those desiring the Lord’s day! Why is this Lord’s day for you? It is darkness, not light,

Amos 5:19.text: as when someone flees from a lion and a bear falls upon him, then leaps into his house, braces his hands upon the wall, and a snake bites him.

Amos 5:20.text: Is not the Lord’s day darkness rather than light, gloom that has no brightness in it?

Amos 5:21.text: “I have hated and rejected your festivals, and I certainly will not smell a pleasing scent in your festal gatherings,

Amos 5:22.text: because even if you bring Me whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not receive them, and I will not look upon the salvation offering of your display.

Amos 5:23.text: Remove from Me the sound of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your instruments,

Amos 5:24.text: and judgment shall roll as water, and righteousness as an impassable torrent.

Amos 5:25.text: Did you offer Me slaughtered offerings and sacrifices in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?

Amos 5:26.text: You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, their figures that you made for yourselves.

Amos 5:27.text: I will deport you beyond Damascus,” says the Lord; God Almighty is His name.

Amos 6:1.text: Woe to those who despise Zion and trust in Samaria’s mountain! They harvested the firstfruits of nations and entered themselves. House of Israel,

Amos 6:2.text: all of you cross over and see; pass from there to Emath Rabba, and go down from there to Geth of foreigners, the strongest of all these kingdoms, to see whether their borders are greater than your borders.

Amos 6:3.text: You come toward an evil day, drawing near and touching false sabbaths,

Amos 6:4.text: sleeping upon ivory beds and indulging upon your couches, eating young goats from the flocks and milk-fed calves from the herds,

Amos 6:5.text: clapping to the sound of instruments; they reckoned them as lasting, not passing away,

Amos 6:6.text: drinking strained wine and anointing yourselves with the finest perfumes, yet suffering nothing over Joseph’s shattering.

Amos 6:7.text: Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the powerful, and horses’ neighing will be removed from Ephraim.

Amos 6:8.text: For the Lord swore by Himself: “I abhor all Jacob’s arrogance and have hated his regions; I will remove the city with all who inhabit it.”

Amos 6:9.text: If ten men remain in one house, they will die, and those left over will remain.

Amos 6:10.text: Their relatives will take them and force their way to bring their bones out of the house. He will say to those in charge of the house, “Is there anyone else with you?” He will say, “No more.” Then he will say, “Be silent, so as not to name the Lord’s name.”

Amos 6:11.text: For look, the Lord commands, and He will strike the great house with fractures and the small house with cracks.

Amos 6:12.text: Will horses pursue upon rocks? Will they remain silent among females? For you turned judgment into anger and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness,

Amos 6:13.text: rejoicing over nothing, saying, “Did we not acquire horns by our own strength?”

Amos 6:14.text: “For look, I am raising a nation against you, house of Israel, and they will crush you so that you cannot enter Emath, as far as the Wadi of the West.”

Ezekiel 19:1.text: “And you, take up a lament over Israel’s ruler,

Ezekiel 19:2.text: and say: What was your mother? A cub! She came to be among lions; among lions she multiplied her cubs.

Ezekiel 19:3.text: One of her cubs sprang away; he became a lion, learned to seize prey, and ate human beings.

Ezekiel 19:14.text: and fire went out from a rod of her choice parts and devoured her, and there was no rod of strength in her. A tribe is for a parable of lament, and it will become a lament.”

Jeremiah 14:17.text: And you will say this word to them: Bring tears down upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because the daughter of My people was utterly crushed, with a very painful wound.

Jeremiah 14:18.text: If I go out to the plain, behold, those wounded by the sword; and if I enter the city, behold, the pain of famine! For priest and prophet went to a land they did not know.

Deuteronomy 28:62.text: And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were as the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.

Deuteronomy 28:63.text: And it shall be, as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and to multiply you, so shall the Lord rejoice over you to destroy you; and you shall be removed from the land whither you go to inherit it.

Isaiah 55:3.text: Listen with your ears, and follow My ways; listen to Me, and your soul will live amid good things. And I will make with you an everlasting covenant: the holy and sure blessings of David.

Isaiah 55:4.text: Behold, I have given him as a testimony among the nations, a ruler and commander of nations.

Isaiah 55:5.text: Nations that did not know you will call upon you, and peoples that do not know you will flee to you for refuge, because of your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you.

Isaiah 55:6.text: Seek God, and when you find Him, call upon Him; and when He draws near to you,

Hosea 4:15.text: But you, Israel, do not be ignorant; and Judah, do not enter Gilgal or go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.

Jeremiah 21:11.text: House of Judah’s king, hear the Lord’s word.

Jeremiah 21:12.text: House of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning, set things straight, and rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that My anger is not kindled like fire and burns with no one to quench it.

Jeremiah 21:13.text: Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Sor, the level land, you who say, Who will frighten us? Or who will enter our dwelling?

Jeremiah 21:14.text: And I will kindle a fire in her woodland, and it will consume everything around her.

Psalms 96:1.text: Of David, when his land is being established. The Lord has become King! Let the earth exult; let many islands rejoice.

Psalms 96:2.text: Cloud and gloom surround Him; righteousness and judgment are the establishment of His throne.

Psalms 96:3.text: Fire will go ahead before Him and set His enemies aflame all around.

Amos 9:5.text: The Lord, Lord God Almighty, touches the earth and shakes it; all who dwell in it will mourn. Its consummation will rise like a river and descend like Egypt’s river.

Amos 9:6.text: He builds His ascent into heaven and establishes His promise upon the earth; He calls for the sea’s water and pours it upon the earth’s surface. The Lord God Almighty is His name.

Isaiah 25:10.text: For God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moab’s land will be trampled as people tread a threshing floor with wagons,

Isaiah 25:11.text: and he will release his hands, just as he himself brought low for destruction; he will bring low his insolence over what he laid his hands on,

Isaiah 25:12.text: and he will bring low the height of your wall’s refuge, and it will descend to the ground.

Proverbs 9:7.text: One who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves an impious person will bring blame on himself.

Proverbs 9:8.text: Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.

Proverbs 9:9.text: Give a wise person a starting point, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will receive still more.

Deuteronomy 28:30.text: You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Deuteronomy 28:31.text: Your calf shall be slaughtered before your eyes, and you shall not eat thereof; your donkey shall be seized from you, and shall not be restored unto you; your sheep shall be given unto your enemies, and there shall be none to help you.

Deuteronomy 28:32.text: Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another nation, and your eyes shall look upon them and waste away; and your hand shall have no strength.

Deuteronomy 28:33.text: A nation which you do not know shall consume the yield of your land and all your labours; and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days.

Exodus 23:6.text: You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his cause.

Exodus 23:7.text: You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.

Exodus 23:8.text: And you shall receive no gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of those who see, and corrupt righteous words.

Ecclesiastes 3:1.text: For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter beneath heaven.

Ecclesiastes 3:2.text: a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted,

Ecclesiastes 3:3.text: a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to pull down and a time to build,

Ecclesiastes 3:4.text: a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to beat the breast in mourning and a time to dance,

Ecclesiastes 3:5.text: a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing,

Ecclesiastes 3:6.text: a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away,

Ecclesiastes 3:7.text: a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak,

Ecclesiastes 3:8.text: a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.

Romans 12:9.text: Let love be without hypocrisy. Abhor what is evil; cling to what is good.

Romans 12:10.text: In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; take the lead in honoring one another;

Romans 12:11.text: do not be slack in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord;

Romans 12:12.text: rejoice in hope; persevere in affliction; persist in prayer;

Romans 12:13.text: share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.

Deuteronomy 16:18.text: You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.

Deuteronomy 16:19.text: They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.

Deuteronomy 16:20.text: You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.

Jeremiah 9:16.text: Thus says the Lord: Call the women who lament, and let them come; send for the skilled women, and let them speak,

Jeremiah 9:17.text: and let them take up a dirge over you; let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.

Jeremiah 9:18.text: For a voice of lament was heard in Zion: How we suffered misery and were greatly ashamed, because we abandoned the land and threw away our dwellings!

Jeremiah 9:19.text: Hear God’s word now, women, and let your ears receive His mouth’s words; teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor a dirge.

Jeremiah 9:20.text: For death climbed through your windows and entered your land, to wipe out little children outside and young men from the squares.

Exodus 12:12.text: I will go through the land of Egypt that night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both human and animal. Against all the Egyptians’ gods I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.

Exodus 12:13.text: And the blood shall be a sign to you upon the houses in which you are; and I will see the blood, and shelter you; and no plague of destruction shall be among you when I strike the land of Egypt.

Joel 2:1.text: Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,

Joel 2:2.text: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.

Isaiah 24:17.text: Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!

Isaiah 24:18.text: Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.

Zephaniah 1:14.text: For the Lord’s great day is near, near and very swift. The sound of the Lord’s day is bitter and harsh; it is appointed mighty.

Zephaniah 1:15.text: That day is a day of wrath, a day of affliction and constraint, a day of untimely ruin and destruction, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist,

Zephaniah 1:16.text: a day of trumpet and shouting against fortified cities and high corners.

Zephaniah 1:17.text: I will press people hard, and they will walk like the blind because they sinned against the Lord. He will pour out their blood like dust and their flesh like dung.

Zephaniah 1:18.text: Their silver and gold will certainly not rescue them on the day of the Lord’s wrath. In the fire of His jealousy all the earth will be consumed, for He will bring completion and haste upon all the earth’s inhabitants.

Isaiah 1:13.text: you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,

Isaiah 1:14.text: and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.

Isaiah 1:15.text: Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.

Jeremiah 6:19.text: Hear, earth! Behold, I am bringing evils upon this people, the fruit of their turning away, because they did not attend to My words and rejected My law.

Jeremiah 6:20.text: Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba and cinnamon from a distant land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices did not please Me.

Jeremiah 6:21.text: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am placing weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will become weak in it; neighbor and his neighbor will perish.

Ezekiel 26:12.text: He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.

Ezekiel 26:13.text: He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.

Ezekiel 26:14.text: I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.

Isaiah 48:17.text: Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s Holy One: “I am your God. I have shown you how to find the road on which you will walk.

Isaiah 48:18.text: If you had listened to My commands, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like a sea wave.

Isaiah 48:19.text: Your offspring would have become like sand, those born from your belly like the earth’s dust. Even now you will certainly not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before Me.”

Acts 7:42.text: But God turned away and handed them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you offer Me slaughtered victims and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?

Acts 7:43.text: You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, the images you made to worship them. And I will deport you beyond Babylon.’

Luke 16:19.text: Now there was a certain rich man, and he clothed himself in purple and fine linen, enjoying himself in splendor every day.

Luke 16:20.text: And a certain poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gateway, covered with sores

Luke 16:21.text: and longing to be filled with what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

Isaiah 5:7.text: For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is Israel’s house, and the man of Judah a beloved new planting. I waited for it to produce judgment, but it produced lawlessness, not righteousness but an outcry.

Isaiah 5:11.text: Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing strong drink, lingering into the evening, for wine will burn them up!

Isaiah 5:12.text: For with lyre and harp, drums and flutes they drink wine, but they do not look at the Lord’s works or consider the works of His hands.

Isaiah 5:13.text: Therefore My people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and there was a multitude of dead through famine and thirst for water.

Isaiah 22:12.text: The Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping, lamentation, shaving and putting on sackcloth,

Isaiah 22:13.text: but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep to eat meat and drink wine, saying, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”

Isaiah 22:14.text: These things are revealed in the Lord Sabaoth’s ears: “This sin will not be forgiven you until you die.”

Jeremiah 22:1.text: Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,

Jeremiah 22:2.text: and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.

Jeremiah 22:3.text: Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.

Jeremiah 22:4.text: Because if you truly carry out this word, kings sitting upon David’s throne and riding chariots and horses will enter this house’s gates—they, their servants, and their people.

Jeremiah 22:5.text: But if you do not carry out these words, I swear by Myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a desolation.

Amos 3:15.text: and I will confound and strike the colonnaded house along with the summer house. Ivory houses will perish, and many other houses will be added,” says the Lord.

Deuteronomy 8:17.text: Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand have gotten me this great wealth.

Deuteronomy 8:18.text: And you shall remember the Lord your God, for He gives you strength to gain wealth, that He may establish His covenant which the Lord sware unto your fathers, as at this day.

Jeremiah 5:15.text: Behold, I am bringing a nation upon you from far away, house of Israel, says the Lord, a nation whose language’s sound you will not understand.

Jeremiah 5:17.text: and they will devour your harvest and your bread, and devour your sons and daughters, and devour your sheep and calves, and devour your vineyards and fig orchards and olive groves; and with a sword they will thresh your fortified cities, in which you have trusted.

Zephaniah 1:7.text: Revere the Lord God, for the Lord’s day is near. The Lord has prepared His sacrifice and consecrated His invited guests.
